headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust paths: Replit Agent can write broadly while OpenBBTerminal can ingest MCP/API content, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs, so if Replit Agent writes attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace or service endpoint, OpenBB may ingest it as trusted input. Replit Agent has broad shell/write access, making such content easy to place. The bridge is plausible but not proven by docs, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Replit Agent writes prompt-like content into a file or service that OpenBBTerminal reads via MCP/API
IF OpenBBTerminal treats file or API content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a dedicated input directory with a strict allowlist of file types
Add a one-line provenance banner to all Replit-generated artifacts
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted folders
Require manual review before OpenBB consumes any Replit-produced output

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and handles secrets. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive financial or secret-bearing content can flow into Replit’s cloud environment. Because Replit Agent has broad network egress and file access, the blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or copied files
IF financial data, licensed data, or secrets are present in those files
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Move sensitive files to a read-protected directory
Rotate any secrets that were ever placed in shared files
Block outbound network access for the Replit workspace during shared-file handling
Review file sync settings before any cross-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs and supports multiple instances. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and state changes can collide without locking. The profiles show no shared lock or coordination primitive, so the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF no external lock or checkout discipline is enforced
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a simple file lock or mutex file
Run a quick diff before merging outputs
Avoid concurrent git operations

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API outputs, and Replit Agent can generate code, configs, or other artifacts inside a persistent Repl. If OpenBB treats Replit output as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or analyses. The pathway exists in default-style workflows, but the profiles do not show direct autonomous external actions, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Replit-produced files or API responses without validation
IF those outputs are then used to drive analysis, code, or operational steps
mitigations: Add a verification step before any downstream use
Require schema checks on exchanged artifacts
Mark Replit outputs as draft until reviewed
Compare critical values against a second source
Stop the pipeline on parse errors or missing fields

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated financial data or secrets are moved into Replit’s environment, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show a matching compliance boundary or DPA, so the safer reading is high.
conditions: IF financial data or secrets are transferred into the Replit workspace
IF the organization requires residency, retention, or DPA controls not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit workspaces
Redact secrets before handoff
Confirm retention settings in both environments
Document the data flow and legal basis
Use synthetic or masked datasets for testing
